newsitem.title: UK: UK bosses' pay lags France and Germany.
newsitem.headline: UK bosses' pay lags France and Germany.

text.p: Senior British bosses are paid less than their counterparts in France and Germany, but they have the highest purchasing power in Europe, a survey said on Wednesday.

Towers Perrin, a large firm of human resources consultants and actuaries, said British executives' pay lags renumeration rates in France, Switzerland, Belgium and Germany, but outstrips top pay in Italy, Spain and the Netherlands.
"British chief executives receive an average total package of 319,604 stg while French and German counterparts receive 380,903 stg and 321,414 stg respectively," said the survey.
Top level pay is a contentious issue in Britain.

The press and some politicians have attacked so-called "fat cats", bosses of newly privatised ultilities in particular, for awarding themselves very generous pay increases and performance related packages.
In the worldwide league table of top pay, the UK lies tenth out of 21 countries surveyed.
However, when it comes to purchasing power, Britain leads the pack with the highest spending power in Europe.
Using a base of 100 for the U.S. which tops the worldwide table, the British bosses have net purchasing power of 57, while France has 44 and Germany 46.
"But in global terms, European purchasing power has declined sharply in comparison with the U.S. since last year," the survey said.
And despite earning less than French and German bosses, British executive have leapfrogged both of them in terms of take home (after-tax) pay.
"The UK is now ranked ninth , up from 11th in 1995. Average net pay is 119,546 stg. US chief executives fare better with average net pay of 119,752," the survey said.
Average pay increases in 1996 were 5.5 percent, second in Europe only to Italian bosses with rises of 6.1 percent.
Across the rest of Europe and in the U.S. salary increases were more modest at between 3.0 and 4.0 percent."
